scope.purpose: Provide conservative slicer starting values for the ZEIM nozzle picker.
scope.priority: Manufacturer profiles first; derived geometric limits and conservative defaults second.
scope.validation: These are starting values. Calibrate flow, pressure advance, temperature, and retraction for each printer, filament, and nozzle before production use.

layer_height.rule: Keep nominal layer height at or below 80% of nozzle diameter; a practical detailed range is 20-70% of nozzle diameter.

line_width.rule: Start near nozzle diameter; use approximately 75-150% of nozzle diameter as the practical range.

flow.rule: Set flow ratio near 1.0 only after calibration; use the printer/filament manufacturer profile where available.
flow.note: Volumetric flow is limited by hotend, material, temperature, and nozzle diameter, not by nozzle size alone.

0.2.use_case: Fine detail, small text, miniature features

material_notes.PLA: Use manufacturer profile where available; Creality documents Hyper PLA at 0.98 flow ratio and 3 mm3/s maximum volumetric speed for K1-family 0.2 mm profiles.
material_notes.PETG: Use manufacturer profile where available; Creality documents CR-PETG at 0.97 flow ratio and 2.5 mm3/s maximum volumetric speed for K1-family 0.2 mm profiles.
material_notes.TPU: Start conservatively; small nozzles increase back-pressure and make flexible filament more difficult.
material_notes.ABS/ASA: Use an enclosure and reduced cooling; validate warping and emissions safety before use.

0.4.use_case: General-purpose default; balanced detail, strength, and speed

Creality.documented: 0.4 mm is the standard/default K1-family nozzle size.

printers: Most Bambu Lab printers ship with 0.4 mm
Most Prusa FDM printers use 0.4 mm as the default

material_notes.PLA: Start with the printer manufacturer's PLA profile; calibrate flow and pressure advance.
material_notes.PETG: Use manufacturer PETG profile; expect slightly slower, more viscous printing than PLA.
material_notes.TPU: Use a direct-drive extruder where possible; print slowly and disable or minimize retraction initially.
material_notes.ABS/ASA: Use an enclosure, controlled cooling, and a heated bed; validate warping and ventilation.

0.6.use_case: Faster functional prints, thicker walls, better layer bonding

Creality.documented: Available nozzle size; use a tested profile and calibrate.

material_notes.PLA: Can use higher volumetric flow than 0.4 mm, but remain within the hotend's measured limit.
material_notes.PETG: Use a conservative speed until flow is calibrated; PETG can string more at high temperatures.
material_notes.TPU: Possible but more difficult; use slow speeds and a direct-drive extruder.
material_notes.ABS/ASA: Use an enclosure; larger beads can improve layer bonding but increase shrinkage-related stress.

Creality.documented: Available nozzle size; validate before production use.

material_notes.PLA: Best for rapid prototypes and thick-walled parts; detail and small holes suffer.
material_notes.PETG: Use conservative speeds and calibrated flow; large beads can trap heat and sag.
material_notes.TPU: Not recommended as a beginner configuration; flexible filament plus a large nozzle is difficult to control.
material_notes.ABS/ASA: Use an enclosure and gradual cooling; large cross-sections increase warp risk.

1.0.use_case: Very large, low-detail parts; maximum throughput

printers: K1-family compatible nozzles are available from third-party sellers
Creality.documented: Treat as advanced/community-supported unless the exact printer profile is published by Creality.

printers: Not listed among Bambu's typical four nozzle sizes

material_notes.PLA: Use only when print time matters more than detail; validate hotend flow and part cooling.
material_notes.PETG: Advanced use; large beads hold heat and are prone to sagging.
material_notes.ABS/ASA: Advanced use; high shrinkage stress and warp risk make this a poor default.

Creality K1 family.note: Creality documents official 0.2 mm parameter profiles for K1, K1 Max, K1C, and K1 SE; 0.4 mm is the standard default. Larger sizes are commonly available, but use tested profiles and calibration.

Bambu Lab.note: Bambu documents 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 mm nozzle sizes; 0.4 mm is the common shipped default.

Prusa.note: Prusa documents nozzle-diameter effects and supports alternate nozzle sizes; 0.4 mm is the common default. Confirm the exact nozzle options for the specific printer model before exposing them in the picker.

PLA.notes: Use manufacturer profile first; PLA is generally the easiest material for nozzle comparison.

PETG.notes: Use manufacturer profile first; reduce speed if stringing, poor layer bonding, or under-extrusion appears.

TPU.notes: Use slow speeds, minimal retraction, and a direct-drive extruder where possible; calibrate carefully.

ABS/ASA.notes: Use an enclosure, heated bed, and controlled cooling; validate warping, fumes, and ventilation.
